# INT8 latency across machines (supplementary, post-test; generated by scripts/analyze_hw_latency.py)

6 machine(s). Each timed the same deployment variants of four architectures (participant 1, seed 0): one prediction at a time (batch 1) on one CPU thread. INT8 means 8-bit integer weights and activations; "first two layers swapped" runs EEGNet's spatial convolution before its temporal one, which gives the same predictions (int8 study) with far fewer multiply-adds. FP32 is the original 32-bit floating-point graph. Post-test and exploratory: timing does not change any accuracy.

## Machines and the integer instructions their CPUs report

| machine | CPU | instruction set | integer extensions present | checked, absent | ONNX Runtime | load average at start (1 min) | rounds x calls |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | ---: | --- |

| c0309 | Intel(R) Xeon(R) Gold 6140 CPU @ 2.30GHz | x86-64 | AVX2, AVX-512F | AVX-512 VNNI, AVX-VNNI, AMX-INT8, AMX-TILE, asimddp, i8mm | 1.31.1 | 45.9 | 15 x 500 |
| c0315 | Intel(R) Xeon(R) Gold 6140 CPU @ 2.30GHz | x86-64 | AVX2, AVX-512F | AVX-512 VNNI, AVX-VNNI, AMX-INT8, AMX-TILE, asimddp, i8mm | 1.31.1 | 53.5 | 15 x 500 |
| c151411 | AMD EPYC 9654 96-Core Processor | x86-64 | AVX2, AVX-512F, AVX-512 VNNI | AVX-VNNI, AMX-INT8, AMX-TILE, asimddp, i8mm | 1.31.1 | 253.5 | 15 x 500 |
| c151417 | AMD EPYC 9654 96-Core Processor | x86-64 | AVX2, AVX-512F, AVX-512 VNNI | AVX-VNNI, AMX-INT8, AMX-TILE, asimddp, i8mm | 1.31.1 | 267.7 | 15 x 500 |
| intel-no-avx512 | Intel(R) Xeon(R) CPU E5-2680 v3 @ 2.50GHz | x86-64 | AVX2 | AVX-512F, AVX-512 VNNI, AVX-VNNI, AMX-INT8, AMX-TILE, asimddp, i8mm | 1.31.1 | 33.4 | 15 x 500 |

AVX-512 VNNI and AVX-VNNI (x86), AMX (Intel's matrix tiles), and DotProd and I8MM (Arm) are instructions that multiply and add 8-bit integers in hardware; AVX2 and AVX-512F are general vector instructions. A record lists only the extensions its operating system reports, so a missing entry is not proof of absence.

## Is the original INT8 graph slower than FP32?

- m4-int8-study (Apple M4): slower than FP32 for 4 of 4 architectures; INT8 takes 1.27x to 1.32x the FP32 time.
- c0309 (Intel(R) Xeon(R) Gold 6140 CPU @ 2.30GHz): slower than FP32 for 4 of 4 architectures; INT8 takes 2.92x to 3.25x the FP32 time.
- c0315 (Intel(R) Xeon(R) Gold 6140 CPU @ 2.30GHz): slower than FP32 for 4 of 4 architectures; INT8 takes 2.97x to 3.30x the FP32 time.
- c151411 (AMD EPYC 9654 96-Core Processor): slower than FP32 for 4 of 4 architectures; INT8 takes 2.33x to 2.42x the FP32 time.
- c151417 (AMD EPYC 9654 96-Core Processor): slower than FP32 for 4 of 4 architectures; INT8 takes 2.33x to 2.48x the FP32 time.
- intel-no-avx512 (Intel(R) Xeon(R) CPU E5-2680 v3 @ 2.50GHz): slower than FP32 for 4 of 4 architectures; INT8 takes 2.11x to 2.26x the FP32 time.

Slower for every architecture on: m4-int8-study, c0309, c0315, c151411, c151417, intel-no-avx512. Faster for every architecture on: no machine. Mixed: no machine.

## Is the layer-swapped INT8 graph faster than FP32 everywhere?

Yes, on every machine and architecture measured (24 pairs): it takes 0.24x to 0.95x the time of the original FP32 graph on the same machine.
Against the FP32 graph with the same swap (the fastest FP32 version measured), the swapped INT8 graph is faster in 4 of 24 pairs, taking 0.55x to 2.74x its time.

## Reading the result

The original INT8 graph is slower than FP32 on every machine, including those whose CPUs multiply 8-bit integers in hardware (m4-int8-study, c151411, c151417). That points at the path ONNX Runtime takes for this graph (its grouped spatial convolution), not at a missing 8-bit unit in one chip: quantizing to 8 bits did not by itself make this model faster on any machine measured.

Notes:

- The M4 reference comes from scripts/int8_study.py (cycling through 100 session-1 trials); the other machines ran scripts/hw_latency.py (64 trials). Both time with mibci.timing: interleaved rounds, the median of the per-round medians.
- The M4 relevance-8 row is the int8 study's proposed-8 graph: for participant 1, seed 0, both rules chose the same eight electrodes and the archived models give identical predictions.
- These are compute times for one prediction. They do not include the 2-second EEG window a prediction needs, and machines shared with other jobs (see the load average) add noise; ratios within one machine are more reliable than times across machines.
